contentFull:
Light disc fertiliser as basis for fertiliser robot

 15-10 | Smart farming | News

LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

Herre Bartlema with the prototype of the light disc fertiliser. The idea is to further develop the technology into an autonomous vehicle that applies liquid fertilisers and refills the tank itself. Photos: Martin Smits

A simple disc fertiliser can form the basis for a robot that places liquid fertilisers in the root zone. The prototype exists. Autonomous driving and filling still have to be developed.

A light disc fertiliser as the basis for a robot that places liquid fertilisers in the soil. That idea was shown on 11 September in Zwartebroek, Gelderland, during the demo day organised by Coöperatie Gelderse Vallei Kunstmestvrij. The technology has a simple design, but still has to be developed further into an autonomous machine. In the prototype, the discs drive a roller pump that handles the fertiliser dosage. This links the movement of the discs with the operation of the pump. The discs place the liquid fertiliser in the soil. The starting point is a light machine that applies plant nutrition in the root zone at the moment the crop needs it.

Light and electric

Herre Bartlema, chairman of the Dutch Centre for the Development of Circular Precision Fertilisation (NCOK), sees opportunities to combine this technology with an electrically powered, autonomous vehicle. A heavy machine is not needed for the principle shown. The prototype mainly shows how the fertilisation technology can be implemented simply and in a lightweight form. A self-driving and fertilising robot is therefore not yet a practical reality.

Filling the tank could also be autonomous, via a docking station. The machine could then take in fertiliser before going back to work. That is part of the idea. The setup shown does not yet provide clarity on the design of the docking station or its connection to the vehicle.

The discs drive a roller pump that doses the fertiliser. The simple setup makes possible a light fertiliser that places liquid plant nutrition in the soil.Dosing in the root zone

Bartlema has been an advocate of precision fertilisation and emission reduction for years. He expects renure to deliver a large supply of fast-acting liquid plant nutrition. According to him, that fertiliser must reach the root zone at the right moment. The light disc fertiliser fits that idea: targeted application in the soil rather than surface spreading.

Practical feasibility and affordability remain points for attention. The prototype offers a glimpse of the technology, but data on working width, tank capacity, forward speed and capacity are missing from the description. No results are mentioned either on dosing accuracy or performance under different soil conditions. The idea exists; the step towards a fertiliser robot has yet to follow.

translationZh:
一款简单的圆盘施肥机可以构成将液体肥料施入根区的机器人的基础。原型已经存在。自主行驶和自动加料仍需开发。

以轻型圆盘施肥机为基础，开发一种将液体肥料施入土壤的机器人。这一想法于9月11日在海尔德兰省Zwartebroek展示，活动由Coöperatie Gelderse Vallei Kunstmestvrij组织的演示日。该技术设计简单，但仍需进一步开发为自主机器。在原型中，圆盘驱动一个滚柱泵来处理肥料计量。这将圆盘的运动与泵的操作联系起来。圆盘将液体肥料施入土壤。出发点是一台轻型机器，在作物需要时向根区施用植物营养。

**轻量化和电动化**

荷兰循环精准施肥发展中心（NCOK）主席Herre Bartlema看到了将这项技术与电动自主车辆结合的机会。所展示的原理不需要重型机器。原型主要展示了施肥技术如何以简单和轻量的形式实现。因此，自动驾驶和施肥机器人尚未成为现实。

通过对接站，加料也可以自主完成。机器然后可以在返回工作前补充肥料。这是想法的一部分。所展示的设置尚未明确对接站的设计或其与车辆的连接。

圆盘驱动一个滚柱泵来计量肥料。简单的设置使得轻型施肥机能够将液体植物营养施入土壤。

**根区计量**

Bartlema多年来一直倡导精准施肥和减排。他预计renure将提供大量速效液体植物营养。据他所说，这种肥料必须在正确的时间到达根区。轻型圆盘施肥机符合这一想法：有针对性地施入土壤，而不是表面撒施。

实际可行性和可负担性仍然是关注点。原型提供了技术的一瞥，但描述中缺少工作幅宽、罐容量、前进速度和 capacity 的数据。也没有提到计量精度或不同土壤条件下的性能结果。想法存在；迈向施肥机器人的一步尚未到来。
